title: model
description: A model record (RFC-020), optional: data/models/<model_id>.yaml. A model is onboarded once for the project and used by any eval's arms: its deployment on every machine that runs it, what it can do, the settings chosen for it and the smoke behind them. `aliases` are the ids runs record for it (params.model); the arms page's weights filter and the catalog's Models page read the records. A record of kind `code` (the fleet's feedback 27) is code under test rather than a model: its `repo` and its `versions` (each a commit, when it ran in production, and, once checked, how faithfully a replay reproduces what production recorded); an arm names it with `model_record:` like any record.

model_id.description: The record's id: its file's name.

actor.description: Who acted (RFC-027): a person, or an agent and the person it acted for. A recorded claim, not an identity.

for.description: the person an agent acted for

name.description: A display name, when the id is not enough.

aliases.description: The ids runs record for this model (params.model): a gateway alias, an Ollama tag, a Hugging Face repo.

weights.description: open: the weights can be downloaded; proprietary: only its vendor serves it.

licence.description: The licence of open weights, as its publisher states it.

capabilities.description: What the model can do, as measured.

reasons.description: It reasons before answering by default.

reasoning_off.description: The setting that turns reasoning off ("reasoning_effort: none"), or null when it cannot be turned off.

deterministic.description: The same request twice gave the same output on the machine it was checked on.

outputs.description: An ML model's labels or output shape.

settings.description: How the model is set up whatever the task, passed to every arm that names the record (an arm may override them): an LLM's reasoning; an ML model's device, precision and batch size. A reply cap or a call limit is a task's: the arm sets it.

settings_why.description: One line per setting: why it was chosen.

accepted.description: Flag kinds (reasoning, format, ...) a person accepted as a known property of the model, each with why: onboarding and arm smokes report them as accepted, not as something to fix (gpt-oss cannot stop reasoning).

repo.description: kind code: where the code lives (a git URL or a path), as a person would clone it.

checkout.description: kind code: a local git checkout of `repo` a replay reads its versions from with git archive (relative to the project; RFC-030), when `repo` is a URL. Never written to.

versions.description: kind code: the versions of the code under test, oldest first.

deployed.description: When this version ran in production: [{from, to}] (ISO times; `to` absent while it still runs).

dated_by.description: How `from` was dated (RFC-031 X2): the host's own pull time, or the commit's time when the pull is no longer recorded (approximate: a host's reflog keeps 90 days).

note.description: What changed in this version, in a sentence.

faithfulness.description: How faithfully a replay of this version reproduces what production recorded (R): agreed of items, when, the run.
